title: Rust native-address documentation still labels exact 0200 prefix as /7
description: Rust production code constructs and routes native addresses with byte 0 exactly 0x02, matching the resolved 0200::/8 profile, but lichen-core/src/addr.rs, lichen-gateway/src/config.rs, and gateway trust docs still describe 0200::/7 and /7 dispersion. This contradicts API invariants and can lead callers to admit 0x03 addresses. Update Rust documentation/comments to exact /8 terminology; do not alter canonical derivation bytes.
close_reason: Fixed: the three named files (addr.rs, config.rs, trust.rs) were already /8-clean; the sole remaining stale site was rust/lichen-node/src/node.rs:198 comment '0200::/7 AddrForKey identity' -> '0200::/8'. Verified no other 0200::/7 variants remain in rust/ (fc00::/7 ULA hits are correct RFC 4193). cargo check -p lichen-node green. 3x delegated codereview (kimi-k3): pass1 found 2 adjacent comment-accuracy nits (stale i72x.2 forward-ref, link-local-arm misstatement) -> filed as a8q1 per protocol; pass2 security PASS (change moves terminology in the secure direction); pass3 edge PASS (last /7 instance, // comment, no rustdoc leak).
